issues.legal_issue: A six-month notice is not required for a release application based on the landlord’s bona fide personal requirement when the application is made more than three years and six months after the purchase of a building occupied by a tenant before its purchase.
material_facts: The tenant’s father had occupied the shop before it was purchased by the landlord, and the purchase occurred after the rent-control law commenced.
The landlord applied for release of the shop long after purchasing it, and no six-month notice was served on the tenant.
The lower courts found that the landlord bona fide required the shop for personal occupation.
issues.conclusion: The first proviso to Section 21(1) does not require six months’ notice once more than three years and six months have elapsed since the purchase; the absence of notice did not make the release application unmaintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21(1)(a) and its first proviso must be read harmoniously and in light of the statute’s purpose. The proviso protects tenants against transfers made to create grounds for eviction and gives them notice of the landlord’s requirement, but it is not intended to be a permanent restriction on a purchaser’s rights. Read as a whole, it bars a release application during the initial three-year period and requires notice at least six months before an application made within the period that follows; it does not require notice after three years and six months have elapsed. The Court relied on the principles of statutory interpretation in Union of India v. Filip Tiago De Gama of Vedem Vasco De Gama and the protective purpose of rent-control legislation discussed in Mangat Raj v. Kidar Nath.

rule.if: tenant_occupied_before_purchase and purchase_after_rent_law_commenced and release_application_for_landlord_occupation and more_than_three_years_and_six_months_elapsed and not six_month_notice_served

predicates.tenant_occupied_before_purchase: A tenant occupied the building before the landlord purchased it.
predicates.purchase_after_rent_law_commenced: The landlord purchased the building after the rent-control law had commenced.
predicates.release_application_for_landlord_occupat: The landlord applied for release of the building for the landlord’s or a family member’s occupation.
predicates.more_than_three_years_and_six_months_ela: More than three years and six months elapsed between the purchase and the release application.
predicates.six_month_notice_served: The landlord served the tenant with notice at least six months before the release application.

issues.definition: When a tenant occupied the building before a post-commencement purchase and the landlord applies for release for occupation after more than three years and six months, the application is not barred merely because no six-month notice was served.

issues.legal_issue: A release order based on the landlord’s bona fide personal requirement may be upheld when that requirement has been proved and the lower courts have concurrently found it established.
material_facts: The landlord sought release of the shop for personal occupation.
The landlord proved the claimed bona fide requirement, and the Prescribed Authority, the appellate court, and the High Court upheld that finding.
The tenant appealed against the eviction order.
issues.conclusion: The Court found no substance in the appeal and declined to interfere with the eviction order.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21(1)(a) permits eviction where the building is bona fide required by the landlord for occupation by the landlord or a member of the landlord’s family. The Court held that the landlord was required to prove that ground and noted that it had been successfully proved and upheld by the appellate court.

predicates.appeal_from_eviction_order: The tenant brought an appeal challenging an eviction order.
predicates.landlord_bona_fide_need_proved: The landlord proved a bona fide requirement for occupation by the landlord or a family member.
predicates.lower_courts_concurrently_found_need: The lower courts concurrently found that the landlord’s bona fide requirement was established.

issues.definition: When a tenant appeals an eviction order and the landlord’s bona fide occupation requirement has been proved and concurrently found by the lower courts, the eviction order is upheld.
